title: fix: retry the other Azure region, then OpenAI direct, when Azure GPT Image refuses
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Since 11:31 UTC on 2026-09-29, `gpt-image-1.5` on `myceli-prod-img-15-swedencentral` has returned 404 `DeploymentNotFound` (and sometimes a 408 timeout). Azure still shows the deployment as `Succeeded`. Each request went to a single region, and only a 429 triggered the OpenAI direct fallback, so every Sweden request failed with a 502 (monitor: 0% success across 21 requests in the last hour).

- A 429 or 404 from one Azure region now retries the model's other Azure region. OpenAI direct (the registry fallback in `image-fallbacks.ts`) is used only when every region refuses.
- 429 and 404 mean Azure generated nothing, so neither retry can produce a duplicate image or double billing. Timeouts and 5xx still end the request, as introduced in #14384.
- The region loop and the OpenAI fallback use one shared rule (`isGPTImageRefusedByAzure`).
- A dead reference image link (which also reports 404) still returns 400 with no retry.
- Tests: a region refusal moves to the other region, a refusal from every region goes to OpenAI, and a dead link doesn't retry.

The Sweden deployment is left in place: both regions use their full 90/90 gpt-image-1.5 quota, and a delete might not give the capacity back.

gist.headline: Another route to the pixels
gist.blurb: If one Azure region refuses a GPT Image request, the other gets a turn. If both refuse, OpenAI direct takes over. Polli appreciates a backup plan.
gist.summary: GPT Image 1.5 requests now try the other Azure region after a 429 or 404, then fall back to OpenAI direct if both regions refuse; dead reference-image links still return 400 without retrying.
gist.impact: Image requests can succeed when one Azure deployment is unavailable, while timeouts and server errors still end the request rather than triggering another generation.
gist.visual_concept: Depict GPT Image routing as two friendly, flower-lined paths to Azure region terminals, with a third path to an OpenAI terminal. Polli guides an image request from a closed first gate toward the open second gate; the third path waits as a backup.

The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she is small-to-medium in the scene, with consistent rounded proportions.
